It does not say members can delete other people's bookings; it says only staff and admins can delete everyone's bookings.

The answer states that a full session refuses new bookings with "No places left", so it never holds more bookings than its capacity. That matches the required fact that there are no more bookings than its capacity. No mustNot items apply.

The answer begins with "No" and says members see only their own bookings on the My bookings page, so both required facts are covered. There are no mustNot items, so nothing prohibited is stated. The extra details about staff, admins and the owner's settings do not contradict the required facts.

The answer names all five required facts: class type, instructor, starts at (date and time), capacity (default 12), and places left (calculated as capacity minus bookings). It also mentions bookings, which is extra, and nothing under mustNot applies.

The answer does not state the required facts. It also says two customers cannot book the same time at once. None of that says outright that a booked appointment occupies the barber's time, so one required fact is missing.

The answer states that an invoice becomes overdue automatically 7 days after its due date, and only if its status is still sent. Both required facts are present, and no mustNot items exist.

The answer says no, other users cannot see your clients, and it explains that everyone sees, changes and deletes only their own records. That covers both required facts ("no" and "each user sees only their own"), and nothing in the answer falls under mustNot, which is empty.

The answer covers outstanding, overdue, paid and latest invoices, but it says only "invoiced" rather than "invoiced by month". The required fact is a monthly breakdown, and the answer never mentions one. It therefore misses one of the required facts.

The answer explicitly states that once an invoice is sent or paid it can no longer be edited and can only be credited, which matches the required fact. No mustNot conditions exist, so none are violated.

The answer covers staff and mail and push (email plus push notifications), but it never mentions the kitchen, which is a required fact under must. It says every staff member is notified and does not say the kitchen is told, so one required fact is missing. No mustNot items exist.

Inget under mustNot gäller, eftersom listan är tom. Tillägget om inloggade användare motsäger inte de obligatoriska fakta.

The answer says decline sets the order's status to declined, which covers the first required fact. It also says the action asks for a reason and that staff are asked to say why the order is being declined, which covers the second. No mustNot items are listed, so none are violated.

The answer hedges with "I don't know" instead of saying plainly that visitors cannot see who is selling an item. It does note that no seller field appears in an item's details, but it never concludes that the owner is not shown. It also suggests that the For sale page lets people contact the owner by mail, which muddies the point. So it does not clearly state either required fact.

The answer says photos are reviewed and an item waits until its photos are approved (photos wait for approval), and that the Review page used for approval is admin-only (an administrator approves them). No mustNot conditions apply.
The answer says any signed-in user, including members, can add items. It does not say that only administrators can add items, so it does not state the required fact and in fact contradicts it.
The answer says every incident state is public, which covers 'all of them', and it lists investigating, identified, monitoring and resolved. No mustNot items exist, so none are violated.

The answer mentions all three required facts: programs can read and change components and incidents via a key, they can run the resolve action (marking an incident as over), and AI assistants can use the API too. No mustNot items exist, so none are violated.

The answer says yes, explains that the Slack slash command (incoming chatCommand) creates an Incident from the typed text, and states the status is investigating. All three required facts are covered, and nothing falls under mustNot.

The answer covers all three required facts: it creates a new SupportCase (a new case), sets its status to open, and sends the customer the mail "We got your request", which tells them the request was received. The mustNot list is empty, so nothing is prohibited.
The answer says that users with the agent or admin role can close a case, which covers both required facts (agents and administrators). Nothing is listed under mustNot, so no forbidden claims apply.

The answer says a case must have an assignee when its status is in progress or closed, which matches the required fact "när det pågår eller är stängt". The extra detail about open and reopened cases doesn't contradict it, and there are no mustNot items.

The answer says no, the assistant cannot delete tasks, and states that its role only adds and changes tasks and notes and never deletes. That covers both required facts, and there are no mustNot items to violate.
The answer names all three required roles (admin, member, assistant), and the mustNot list is empty, so nothing in the answer is prohibited.

The answer mentions the "Publish and share" button in Studio's header, names "Publish live" under the Publish section, and says that in a sandbox publishing needs an invite. All three required facts are present, and there are no mustNot items.

The answer does not state either required fact. It never says that once the app is live a custom domain can be set up, and it never mentions an A record and a TXT record. It does not mention a price for domains, so it avoids the mustNot, but it still misses both must items.

The answer states all required facts: it spells out "Model Context Protocol", says AI assistants connect to the app and use it as tools, gives the /mcp address, and says the same keys are used. No mustNot items exist, so nothing is violated.

The answer states all three required facts: only an administrator can make a key, it is done on the users page (called the Team page in the status starter), and the key is shown once. No mustNot items exist, so none are violated.

The answer says Ask is the app's assistant that anyone signing in can ask questions, which loosely covers the assistant idea, but it misses the required facts. It does not say Ask is a panel in the app, and it does not say the questions are about the records. It also never says Ask reads only what the person may read; it says only that it answers without changing anything, which is a different claim. It adds a CLI command instead.

The answer says pricing and plans are not yet set and that the hosted version is a free private beta, so both required facts are covered. It gives no monthly price and no per-app price. The only figure is about €0.002 for seven everyday changes to a small hosted model, which is an AI provider charge rather than a hosting price.

The answer only covers Export CSV on list pages. It never mentions the "Download everything (.zip)" option or that it includes code, history, data and uploads, so two of the three required facts are missing.

The answer says the app's details don't say where data is physically kept, and it never mentions Sweden or that backups are in the same region. It describes the /data volume and the 2 GB storage limit instead, so both required facts are missing.

The answer opens with "Yes", mentions Docker (the app has a Dockerfile and runs anywhere Docker runs), and names the command "smithable deploy --target docker". All three required facts are present and there are no forbidden facts.

The answer says no AI model is needed, and it states that everything in Getting started works without one, including starters, Studio, every operation, deploy and backup. That covers both required facts: "no" and "operations need no model". No forbidden facts are listed under mustNot.
The answer states that a sandbox started without signing up lasts two hours, which is the required fact. No mustNot conditions exist, so nothing disqualifies it.

The answer covers all three required facts: Import is on the Customers list page, it reads a CSV file, and the user should save the Excel sheet as CSV via Save as. It never claims xlsx files are read directly; it says the opposite, that they must be converted to CSV. Extra details such as column matching and undo do not contradict any requirement.

The answer states the 1,000 recipients a month per account limit, but it omits the required fact of 100 recipients a day per app. Since both facts under must are needed, it fails.

The answer states the €2 a month allowance and says that changes made through forms, code, and words the built-in rules understand still work once the allowance is used up. Both required facts are present, and there are no mustNot items to violate.

The answer mentions both required facts: opening the Publish and share page from the Studio header, and clicking Publish live in the Publish section. There are no mustNot items, so nothing is violated.

The answer mentions the "Sign in with Google" page (as the docs source), which loosely covers the first must item. But it never says anything about "under Connections", so that required fact is missing. Since every must item has to be stated, the answer is not right.
The answer states that staging is a separate copy of the app with its own data, which is the only required fact. No mustNot items exist, so none are violated.
The answer mentions downloading everything as a .zip and a one-time transfer link valid for seven days, covering both required facts, and nothing in mustNot is violated.

The answer states that each app gets 2 GB of storage in total, which matches "2 GB per app". It also says that space includes the photos uploaded to it, which covers "uploaded files included". The mustNot list is empty, so nothing is violated.

The answer includes /mcp, but it never says the key comes from the Team page. It only says $KEY is the assistant's key, that the key is shown in step 2, and that it should have the assistant role. The required fact about a key from the Team page is missing.

The answer covers all three required facts and avoids the forbidden one. It says the starter's timer runs a week after the due date and can move a sent invoice to overdue. It says the only invoice mail is "Your invoice", sent when Mark sent runs. It tells the user to press Mark paid. The answer does not state any of the required facts. The answer says Claude Code cannot delete anything (including notes), that it can add and change tasks and notes (plus complete or reopen tasks), and that it can read everything. That covers all three required facts, and there are no mustNot items to violate.
